findings.description: The relay exception to defaultCache, the IllegalArgumentException for contentLength < -1 and the 204/304 framing rules are documented only on the internal DefaultResponse javadoc. The public Response.relay javadoc says nothing about them, docs/api has no relay entry at all (grep -rn relay docs/api returns nothing), and docs/api/static.md:156 / response.md:120 / defaults.md:97 still state that defaultCache fills every response without Cache-Control. CLAUDE.md requires docs/api to change with the API.
findings.suggested_fix: Document relay (Express analogue, Java/Kotlin examples) in docs/api/response.md (+en), add the relay exception to the defaultCache paragraphs, and add @throws IllegalArgumentException plus the defaultCache/204 rules to Response.relay javadoc.

evidence.intent_output: FR-HTTP-037 AC-4 (length < -1 -> IAE, stream closed) and AC-8 (committed -> ISE, stream closed); the ACs do not order the two

findings.drop_reason: Both ACs hold in their own conditions; the overlap is unspecified, and argument-first validation matches res.stream (null contentType -> NPE before the state check). Stream ownership is honoured.
findings.title: relay(in, <-1) on an already committed response throws IllegalArgumentException, not IllegalStateException
findings.description: Argument validation runs before the state check, so a bad length on a committed response reports IllegalArgumentException; the stream is still closed once.
findings.suggested_fix: None required; optionally state the precedence in the javadoc.

findings.drop_reason: Cannot flake toward failure (green path never depends on the sleep); it only bounds detection of a hypothetical async eager copy.
findings.title: AC-7 test relies on Thread.sleep(50) inside the handler
findings.description: pause(50) only gives an asynchronous eager copy time to read; the decisive check (handlerReturned at first read) is deterministic for a synchronous eager copy.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally replace the pause with a latch the source awaits.

findings.drop_reason: AC-6 only requires the connection to close before 5 body bytes arrive; the looser check still pins that intent.
findings.title: FR-ENGINE-014 AC-6 test also passes when the server sends no head at all
findings.description: The else-branch accepts a connection closed before any head; a server that refuses the request outright would also pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Optionally assert the head arrives (TinyHttpd 3.1.1 commits before the copy) to pin Content-Length: 5 on the wire.

findings.drop_reason: Abort is fired before closeInput in runTransfer, so the latch already orders the normal case; the window is a reasonable bound for an absence check.
findings.title: settlesAt uses a fixed 300 ms window to prove onAbort never/only once runs
findings.description: A listener fired later than 300 ms after the source closes would be missed (false pass), not a flake.
findings.suggested_fix: None; an absence assertion needs a bounded window.

clean_code.description: begin() decides whether to apply defaultCache from the relayed field that startBody sets immediately before calling it; the policy is passed through mutable instance state instead of a begin parameter (e.g. begin(length, body, applyDefaultCache)), and the field outlives its only use.
startBody gained a fifth, boolean parameter that switches two unrelated policies (Content-Length retention on 304 and the defaultCache bypass); three call sites now pass bare true/false literals.
ResponseRelayTest.count(...) and ResponseRelayFramingTest.values(...) (ResponseRelayFramingTest.java:415-423) are the same case-insensitive header scan written twice in the same package.

Two anonymous close-counting ByteArrayInputStream subclasses with the same shape; a small named helper would do.
